hero.title: Mercedes-Benz M111 Engine - Replacement Cost, Problems & Compatibility
hero.description: The M111 is Mercedes-Benz’s legendary 1.8-litre to 2.3-litre inline-4 petrol engine, famous for introducing the "Kompressor" (supercharger) to the mainstream lineup. Fitted to the W202 C-Class, W210 E-Class, W208 CLK, and R170 SLK, reconditioned M111 engines typically start from £1,500 , serving as a highly sought-after, robust unit for classic Mercedes restorations and daily-driven vintage hosts.

costGuide.title: Mercedes-Benz M111 Engine Replacement Cost (UK)
costGuide.labourLine: Fitting an M111 engine typically takes 8-12 hours at £65-£85/hr (independent) - confirm exact labour when comparing quotes.
paragraphs: What genuinely moves the price for this engine is the condition of the balance shaft gears, timing chain tensioner, and (on Kompressor models) the supercharger coupler and snout bearings. Because the M111 is a robust but aging unit, recon specialists will typically replace the balance shaft assembly, fit a new timing chain kit, and refurbish or replace the Kompressor unit as standard to prevent immediate post-installation failures. For a full breakdown of market rates, see our full reconditioned engine cost guide.

failures.title: Mercedes-Benz M111 Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: Balance Shaft Gear Wear - All variants
items.whatHappens: The balance shafts, designed to smooth out inline-4 vibrations, are driven by small gears that can wear or shear over time. This triggers crankshaft position sensor (CPS) error codes, causes a rough idle, misfires, and in severe cases, the broken gear fragments can jam the oil pump or timing chain, leading to catastrophic engine failure.
items.repairVsReplace: If caught early (via CPS codes and rough running), replacing the balance shaft assembly and gears is a known, albeit labour-intensive, repair. If the oil pump or timing has been compromised, a full reconditioned M111 unit is required.

items.title: Kompressor Coupler and Snout Wear - Supercharged variants (.940, .960, .980)
items.whatHappens: The Eaton M45/M62 supercharger uses a plastic/rubber coupler to connect the drive pulley to the internal rotors. Over time, this coupler disintegrates, resulting in a loud rattling or whining noise from the front of the engine and a complete loss of boost pressure. Additionally, the snout bearings can wear, causing oil leaks into the supercharger intake.
items.repairVsReplace: The coupler can be replaced independently as a relatively inexpensive maintenance item. However, if the snout bearings have failed and scored the housing, a full supercharger rebuild or replacement is necessary.

items.title: Timing Chain Tensioner and Guide Wear - All variants
items.whatHappens: While more robust than some later Mercedes engines, the M111's hydraulic timing chain tensioner can lose pressure, and the plastic guide rails can become brittle. This leads to a rattling noise on cold starts and, if ignored, potential chain skip.
items.repairVsReplace: Replacing the tensioner, chain, and guides is a standard, cost-effective preventative maintenance procedure.

failures.goodYearsLine: The M111 is widely regarded as one of the most durable inline-4 engines Mercedes ever produced. Post-1999 units with revised balance shaft gear materials show significantly improved longevity, and units maintained with regular oil changes routinely exceed 250,000 miles without major internal bottom-end issues .

variants.title: M111 Sub-Codes Explained - Which One Is in Your Car?
variants.intro: ═══════════════════════════════════════ INTRO: The M111 family shares the same fundamental DOHC inline-4 block architecture, but displacement and the presence of the Eaton supercharger (Kompressor) vary significantly. Identifying your exact sub-code is mandatory, as fitting the wrong revision can lead to severe mechanical and ECU incompatibility. - Fitted to: C-Class W202 (C 200), E-Class W210 (E 200) - Key technical difference: The base naturally aspirated 2.0L variant, featuring port fuel injection and a focus on smooth, reliable daily driving. - Sub-code-specific failure note: Shares the family failure pattern above; no unique widespread defects beyond standard balance shaft and timing chain wear. - Interchange note: Not a straight swap with Kompressor variants due to different engine mounts, wiring harnesses, and ECU mapping. - Fitted to: C-Class W202 (C 200 Kompressor), CLK-Class W208 , SLK-Class R170 (SLK 200 Kompressor) - Key technical difference: Features the Eaton M45 supercharger, higher compression pistons, and revised engine management to deliver sports-car performance from a 2.0L displacement. - Sub-code-specific failure note: Shares the family failure pattern above; Kompressor coupler degradation is the primary unique wear item. - Interchange note: Requires matching supercharger plumbing, intercooler (on some applications), and specific ECU mapping; not directly interchangeable with NA blocks. - Fitted to: C-Class W202 (C 180 late), C-Class W203 (C 180 early), E-Class W210 (E 200 late) - Key technical difference: Increased displacement to 2.2L (2199cc) for improved low-end torque, often paired with the newer electronic throttle body and revised HFM engine management. - Sub-code-specific failure note: Shares the family failure pattern above; later models feature slightly improved balance shaft gear materials. - Interchange note: Shares the NA architecture but requires matching intake, exhaust, and ECU for the specific chassis application. - Fitted to: C-Class W202 (C 230 Kompressor), E-Class W210 (E 230 Kompressor), CLK-Class W208 , SLK-Class R170 - Key technical difference: The volume-seller high-performance variant, featuring the larger Eaton M62 supercharger, revised cooling, and robust internals to handle the increased thermal load. - Sub-code-specific failure note: Shares the family failure pattern above; the higher continuous boost loads can accelerate snout bearing wear if oil change intervals were extended. - Interchange note: Not interchangeable with 2.0L Kompressor variants without swapping the supercharger, intake manifold, and ECU. - Fitted to: C-Class W203 (C 200 Kompressor), E-Class W210 (E 200 Kompressor late) - Key technical difference: A later evolution of the Kompressor engine, featuring revised engine management, a more efficient supercharger bypass valve, and updated emissions hardware for the transition into the W203 era. - Sub-code-specific failure note: Shares the family failure pattern above; generally considered the most refined and reliable of the M111 Kompressor variants. - Interchange note: Requires specific W203/W210 facelift wiring harnesses and ECU calibration; not a direct drop-in for earlier W202 chassis.

relatives.description: the older 1.8L-2.5L inline-4 that the M111 replaced, sharing the same robust DOHC architecture but lacking the refined port fuel injection and optional Eaton supercharger of the M111 family.

the modern 1.8L-2.0L inline-4 that eventually replaced the M111 across the C-Class and E-Class range, introducing a timing chain-driven balance shaft and updated engine management, though sharing some similar supercharger vulnerabilities on Kompressor models.

the contemporary 2.4L-3.7L V6 that shared the same transitional era of engine management and similar build quality, but in a larger 6-cylinder configuration for flagship and heavier chassis applications.

variants.closing: The engine code is stamped on the right-hand side of the cylinder block, near the oil filter housing. It will also be listed on your V5C logbook under "Engine Capacity" or visible via a VIN decode. Not sure? Enter your registration above for instant confirmation.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement M111 Engine - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used M111 engine makes sense only if it comes with verifiable service history and documented proof of a recent balance shaft gear inspection/replacement and timing chain service. Given the catastrophic risk of balance shaft failure, buying a used unit with unknown history is a significant financial risk.

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: A proper reconditioned M111 engine is the sweet spot for most buyers. A reputable rebuild will proactively address the common failure points by replacing the balance shaft assembly, fitting a new timing chain kit, and rebuilding or replacing the Kompressor unit, giving the engine a fresh, reliable lease on life.

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full M111 engine rebuild is highly justified for classic W202 C 230 Kompressor or R170 SLK restorations where originality, matching numbers, and maximum longevity are required. An upgraded rebuild should include line-boring the block, new pistons/rings, and a balanced crankshaft.

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: Sourcing and fitting through our vetted network ensures your M111 engine is installed by specialists familiar with classic Mercedes DOHC and Kompressor systems, backed by a nationwide warranty.
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: Because the M111 is typically found in W202, W210, W208, and R170 vehicles valued between £1,500 and £8,000+ (with low-mileage Kompressor models commanding significantly higher premiums), a full replacement is generally financially viable. However, if the lowest viable replacement cost exceeds approximately 60% of the vehicle's current market value, evaluate scrap value before committing .

items.question: What is the most common failure on the M111 engine?
items.answer: The most documented issues are balance shaft gear wear, Kompressor coupler degradation on supercharged models, and timing chain tensioner wear. The balance shaft gears can shear and cause catastrophic engine failure or trigger crankshaft sensor errors, while the Kompressor coupler disintegrates over time, resulting in a loud rattle and complete loss of boost pressure. → Get quotes for a rebuilt M111 with these issues resolved

items.question: Which Mercedes models use the M111 engine?
items.answer: The M111 was fitted to the W202 and W203 C-Class (C 180, C 200, C 230 Kompressor), the W210 E-Class (E 200, E 230), the W208 CLK-Class (CLK 200, CLK 230 Kompressor), and the R170 SLK-Class (SLK 200, SLK 230 Kompressor), serving as the definitive 4-cylinder petrol for these chassis between 1993 and 2002. → Check your registration to confirm your exact M111 fitment

items.question: Should I buy a used or reconditioned M111 engine?
items.answer: A reconditioned M111 is strongly recommended over a used unit. A proper rebuild will proactively address the fatal flaws of age by replacing the balance shaft assembly and gears, fitting a new timing chain kit, and rebuilding or replacing the Kompressor unit, whereas a used engine with unknown history risks immediate, catastrophic bottom-end or supercharger failure. → Compare reconditioned M111 engine prices from UK specialists

items.question: What is the difference between M111.920, .940, .950, .960, and .980?
items.answer: The M111.920 is the 2.0L naturally aspirated variant, the .940 is the 2.0L Kompressor (supercharged) variant, the .950 is the 2.2L naturally aspirated variant, the .960 is the 2.3L Kompressor volume-seller, and the .980 is the later 2.2L Kompressor variant with updated emissions hardware. They share the same core block, but the supercharger plumbing, engine mounts, and ECU mapping differ significantly, making them non-interchangeable without extensive modification. → Enter your reg above to identify your exact M111 sub-code ═══════════════════════════════════════
